game: ATL@NYJ Week 13 2025, kickoff 2025-11-30 13:00 ET, NYJ +3, total 38.5, outdoors

script.base: Low-event outdoor game: ATL -3 implies 20.8, NYJ 17.8, total 38.5, so a one-score run-lean rather than a shootout. Cousins is not a runner (2 carries / 8 yards in weeks 10-12). ATL leans on Bijan Robinson (54 carries / 258 yards, about 18 and 86 per game) with Tyler Allgeier mixed in (26/111). Drake London is out, so the pass game is Darnell Mooney (18 targets / 125 yards / 270 air) and Kyle Pitts, not a WR1 shootout. NYJ stays competitive with Justin Fields (16 carries / 97 yards) and Breece Hall (51/185, only 3.63 YPC). Halftime is one score; if ATL leads late they run. Spread is 3.0, not a blowout, so starters should finish.
script.flip1: ATL jumps ahead by two scores, kills the clock with Robinson and Allgeier, and Mooney's routes stall the way a clock-kill stalls WR yards. Robinson rush over survives; Mooney rec yards die.
script.flip2: NYJ runs on ATL's 4.70 YPC defense, Fields scrambles, NYJ leads, and Cousins has to throw. Robinson carries dry up while Mooney and Pitts targets rise. A second version of this flip is an unsaved weather slog that drags both passing games under.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game report, weeks before inactives lock: Drake London Out (knee) vacates 17 targets and 223 yards over weeks 10-12. Next men in the recent target tree are Mooney (18 targets), Pitts (13), Robinson (9), then David Sills (6), Charlie Woerner (4), and Dontario Drummond (3). Casey Washington is not in that L3 target list, so he is not the proven next man. Chris Lindstrom Questionable (foot): if he sits, ATL pressure up, rush efficiency down, more quick throws (Robinson/Pitts catches up, Mooney deep yards down). NYJ CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr. Doubtful (hip) weakens the outside coverage Mooney attacks. NYJ DT Harrison Phillips Questionable (foot) would soften the run fit if inactive. ATL LB Josh Woods Out (hamstring) and Malik Verdon Out (shoulder) help NYJ TE Mason Taylor and Hall as a receiver, not Pitts. Allen Lazard Questionable (neck) is minor Jets WR depth. Final inactives about 90 minutes before kick are not in the pack.

Location splits stand in: NYJ (11 games) YPA left 7.31 (128), middle 5.02 (65), right 7.61 (132), so the Jets are sound in the middle and bleed outside. ATL YPA left 7.16 (129), middle 10.58 (64), right 5.54 (134), so Atlanta bleeds the middle and is best on the right.
matchup.pressure: NYJ blitzes 30%. ATL EPA/dropback is -0.24 vs blitz and +0.08 vs no blitz, so pressure hurts Cousins and cuts Mooney's 15-air-yard shots. ATL blitzes 40%. NYJ EPA/dropback is +0.06 vs blitz and -0.09 vs no blitz, so Fields handles pressure better and checkdowns (Hall, Taylor) are the fit.
matchup.bleeds: NYJ bleeds outside passing (7.31/7.61 YPA) and has allowed 32 passes of 20+ for 344 yards; rush defense is average, 4.47 YPC and 36 runs of 10+. ATL bleeds the middle (10.58 YPA) and the run (4.70 YPC, 35 runs of 10+) and has allowed 28 passes of 20+ for 366 yards.
matchup.overlap: Mooney, the outside high-air receiver, overlaps NYJ's weak left/right and a doubtful outside CB. Pitts does not: NYJ's middle at 5.02 YPA is their strength. On the other side Taylor and Hall's checkdowns overlap ATL's middle bleed, 40% blitz, and two linebackers out. That NYJ overlap was noted and not used as a leg: Taylor's L3 average is 18.3 yards against a 21.5 stand-in (lean plus disagreeing form, so drop), and Hall's receiving line is a 6-yard-floor variance bet.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Lindstrom was inactive, the Jets blitzed, and Atlanta's -0.24 EPA versus blitz pushed Cousins to Pitts and Robinson checkdowns, so Mooney repeated a 15-17 yard game instead of clearing 20.5. The Jets also sold out on Robinson, Allgeier took the cheap yards the way he did in his 57-yard game, and Robinson landed on the 46- or 70-yard side of his recent range because Phillips played. A big early ATL lead would have killed Mooney even if Robinson cashed, which is the correlation break. That counter is real, but it is not stronger than the read: London's 17 targets have to land somewhere, 20.5 is only Mooney's own median, and Robinson's last three rush games were 84, 104, and 70 against a 4.47 YPC run defense. Keep both, tagged to those kills.
slip_story: One story only: ATL in a modest lead or a one-score grind, London's targets condensed onto Mooney, Robinson carrying as the lead back. These two win together in that complementary script. They should not be paired with a game under, with Pitts or Wilson overs, or with a NYJ pass-funnel stack. Hall and Taylor are the other-script (ATL blitz and linebacker) stack and were not used. No bet placed.
